trial_court: District Judge, Dholpur - S.B. Civil Misc. Appeal No. 2015/2007
facts_of_case: Marriage between Mamta and Ramgopal was solemnized on 24th November, 1997. Appellant-wife never treated respondent-husband as her husband and did not allow consummation till filing of application. Respondent-husband sought decree of divorce on ground of cruelty.

legal_principles.principle: Unilateral decision of refusal to have intercourse for considerable period without there being any physical incapacity or valid reason may amount to mental cruelty.
legal_principles.held: The Hon'ble Apex Court observed that (xii) Unilateral decision of refusal to have intercourse for considerable period without there being any physical incapacity or valid reason may amount to mental cruelty.
cited_cases: Samar Ghosh Versus Jaya Ghosh, (2007) 3 Supreme 26

legal_principles.principle: Mental cruelty is the conduct of other spouse which causes mental suffering or fear to the matrimonial life of the other.
legal_principles.held: The Hon'ble Apex Court observed that Mental cruelty is the conduct of other spouse which causes mental suffering or fear to the matrimonial life of the other.
cited_cases: Savitri Pandey Versus Prem Chandra Pandey, (2002) 2 SCC 73

legal_principles.principle: Where there has been a long period of continuous separation, it may fairly be concluded that the matrimonial bond is beyond repair.
legal_principles.held: The Hon'ble Apex Court observed that Where there has been a long period of continuous separation, it may fairly be concluded that the matrimonial bond is beyond repair.
cited_cases: Samar Ghosh Versus Jaya Ghosh, (2007) 3 Supreme 26

outcome.final_order: Decree of divorce dated 11th May, 2007 stands
